entries.summary: Singing hymns in a choir is the only way to use more than one hymn at once, and requires the Supernatural Ability Ceremony.
quotes: singing hymns in a choir is the only way to use more than one Hyperborean hymn at once.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.34 Ceremony

entries.title: Choir Mechanics
entries.summary: How a choir of hymnists produces a one-off free-form effect: a focus character, a storyguide-set Ease Factor, extra level per additional hymn, members adding Communication plus Hymn Ability, a day or more of trance, and a vis cost equal to the Ease Factor.
quotes: Each member of the choir then adds his Communication + Hymn Ability to the focus character's recitation total.
If the effect calls on more than one hymn, increase the level of the Power by 5 for every extra hymn it requires.

entries.title: Choir Recitation Modifier
entries.summary: Table of bonuses to a choir recitation for spending longer than a day performing the hymn, up to a stated maximum.
quotes: This is the maximum bonus possible.

entries.title: Ability: Ceremony (group effort)
entries.summary: The Supernatural Ability that lets a group combine totals: each participant adds Characteristic plus Ability to the focus character's total, with a leader limiting contributors and a penalty if there is no leader; it can also boost seasonal activities.
quotes: Ceremony Bonus: Characteristic + Ability total of each participant
All participants add their totals of the appropriate Characteristic + Ability to the focus character's total.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.36 Ceremony

entries.title: Choir Example
entries.summary: A worked example of six hymnists using a choir to call down a plague, showing the Ease Factor, vis cost and Ceremony Bonus calculation.
quotes: The focus character's recitation total is 8 (Communication 2 + Hymn Iaó 6) with a Ceremony Bonus of 25

entries.title: Hyperborean Enchantments (relics)
entries.summary: How a hymnist crafts relics: an enchantment total against an Ease Factor from the Powers' level, no vis but Warping instead, one season per Power, no size or material limits, plus the things hymn enchanting cannot do. Includes sample relic powers and how profaning or damage strips Powers.
quotes: Enchantment Total: Intelligence + Hymn Ability + modifiers + aura
Enchantment Ease Factor: (total level of Power(s) + modifiers) / 3
Furthermore, instead of using vis, the Hyperborean enchanter Warps his own body, at a rate of 2 Warping Points for every pawn of vis the enchantment would have needed

entries.title: Hyperborean breakthroughs (integration targets)
entries.requires: Hermetic breakthrough research on Hyperborean magic
entries.summary: The minimum breakthrough points required to integrate each aspect of Hyperborean magic (a new Duration, spirit-travel, vis-less permanent magic and enchantment, removing shape, material and size limits, and Ritual effect enchantment), with advice to vary the totals slightly.
quotes: Integrating Vis-less Permanent Magic: 70 breakthrough points
Integrating a New Duration (Minor Breakthrough): 30 breakthrough points

related.text: Ancient Magic Introduction: Hermetic breakthroughs and Insight

entries.title: Hyperborean Integration Process
entries.requires: Hermetic breakthrough research on Hyperborean magic
entries.summary: The five-step process for integrating Hyperborean magic: find a source, gain Insight, incorporate it into a matching effect, research as in the Introduction, and consider the consequences. Each source gives one Insight tied to its most significant Power.
quotes: Each source allows your character to gain one Insight, which permits him to create one specific effect.

entries.title: Hyperborean Insight
entries.requires: Hermetic breakthrough research on Hyperborean magic
entries.summary: Modifiers to the Insight roll from hymn fragments, relics, teachers, knowledge of the Hyperborean language, and combining multiple sources, with the rule that a single source gives Insight only once; includes an example.
quotes: Having only a fragment of a hymn (such as a sacred name or fragments of a prayer string) imposes a –2 penalty on the Insight roll, while a near-complete fragment grants a +2 bonus to the roll.
Having a basic proficiency in Hyperborean grants +1 to the Insight roll for every point the researcher has in the Ability above 4, to a maximum of +3.

entries.title: Consequences of integrating Hyperborean magic
entries.requires: Hermetic breakthrough research on Hyperborean magic
entries.summary: Storyguide advice on what each Hyperborean breakthrough would change in the Order: a 19-year Duration, safer spirit travel, vis-less spells and enchantment (supplementing vis with Warping), unlimited shape, material and size, and enchanting Ritual effects.
quotes: This Breakthrough would allow the enchantment of magical devices by supplementing vis with Warping Points, at a rate of 2 Warping Points for every pawn of vis that would have been needed.

related.text: ArM5 p.161 Aegis of the Hearth

entries.title: Locating the Basilica of Ten Thousand Columns
entries.summary: A shortcut season of research to learn where the basilica lies, resolved by an Order of Hermes Lore stress roll; failure wastes the season and a botch gives a false location.
quotes: Locating the Basilica: Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore + stress die vs. Ease Factor 21

entries.title: The Basilica's Aura
entries.requires: Visiting the Basilica of Ten Thousand Columns
entries.summary: The varying Magic aura levels across the vale and buildings, the waxing and waning with the moon, small Dominion and Divine auras, and a doubling of aura benefit for certain spirit, divination and disease magic.
quotes: any spells cast or supernatural abilities used that relate to the summoning or control of the dead, divining the future, curing or causing disease, or invoking spirits receive double the benefit from the magical aura.

entries.title: Agyieus Pillars (enchanting bonuses)
entries.summary: Agyieus pillars sacred to Apollo may be enchanted and give listed shape and material bonuses for spirits, divination, sunlight, disease and protection.
quotes: The pillars may be enchanted, and provide the following shape and material bonuses: +2 invoking or controlling spirits, +3 divining the future, + 3 summoning sunlight, +5 cause or cure disease, and + 5 protection from hostile spirits.

entries.title: The Altars of Alexander the Great (Arcane Connections)
entries.summary: The altars are linked by dragon lines; casting an Arcane Connection Range spell while touching one treats the other linked shrines, cities and temples as having an Arcane Connection with a bonus multiplier.
quotes: is considered to have an Arcane Connection with a +4 multiplier to the other shrines, cities, or temples connected by the dragon lines.

entries.title: Nekuomanteioi: ghosts as Arcane Connections for necromantic divination
entries.summary: Stat block for the oracular ghosts of the basilica, with a necromancer rule at the end: using such a ghost as an Arcane Connection for Intellego spells to look into the past or future makes the spell a Ritual of higher magnitude and inflicts Warping.
quotes: This increases the magnitude of the spell by 4 if looking into the past, or 5 if looking into the hazy and indistinct future.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.49 Adjuration

entries.title: Spirit guardians of the basilica (manifesting)
entries.requires: Visiting the Basilica of Ten Thousand Columns
entries.summary: The underworld spirits bound to the basilica may be treated as chthonic and mistaken for Infernal creatures by holiness-sensing Virtues, and can spend Might to manifest in a physical form that can be wounded but not killed.
quotes: All of the spirits here can spend 1 Magic Might point to manifest in physical form (and return to spiritual form at will).

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.123 Sense Holiness and Unholiness

entries.title: Hyperborea as a regio
entries.summary: Describes Hyperborea as an island in a multi-level regio that cannot be entered by accident (passwords or an invitation are needed), its inhabitants' Supernatural Powers, and Apollo's visit every nineteen years; includes sidebars on famous Hyperboreans and how to get in.
quotes: Hyperborea is an island hidden in a level 7 regio (although at its highest level it extends to a level 10 regio).

entries.title: Detecting and recognising rune magic
entries.summary: Rune-enchanted objects do not register as magical to Intellego Vim, and active runes are lasting Arcane Connections to the caster, so finding and proving working rune magic takes observation and investigation.
quotes: Because of the way that rune magic changes the nature of its target, objects with active effects do not seem magical to Intellego Vim spells.

entries.title: Dvergar-forged rune items
entries.requires: Contact with the dvergar of Nithavellir
entries.summary: How the faerie dvergar craft rune items on commission: they can do more than human rune wizards, their items resemble Hermetic devices, they work only for the person they were made for, and the price is set afterwards and carries hidden costs.
quotes: items only function for the person for whom they were crafted, though they may be inherited by a blood relative

entries.title: Hermetic Integration of Rune Magic
entries.requires: Hermetic breakthrough research on Rune Magic
entries.summary: After investigating active rune magic, a magus can integrate it into Hermetic theory (a Major Breakthrough) to gain the Hermetic Rune Magic Virtue and the Rune Magic Ability, and learns the three formulas for inscribing a rune spell. Includes the Enchantment Runes sidebar.
quotes: (a Major Breakthrough requiring 45 breakthrough points), producing the new Hermetic Rune Magic Virtue, described below.
There are three ways to formulate a rune spell.

entries.title: Enchantment Runes
entries.summary: How magi with Hermetic Rune Magic invent enchanted devices using the Rune Duration and Inscription Target, and the bonus available to Verditius magi who have the Elder Verditius Runes Mystery.
quotes: they must inscribe the runes onto the item as part of investing the effect.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.127

entries.title: Hermetic Rune Magic: Rune Duration and Inscription Target
entries.summary: The extended mechanic behind the Hermetic Rune Magic Virtue: the Rune Duration and Inscription Target, how and how fast runes are inscribed, casting-total modifiers for hiding or omitting the name and description, the craft-roll alternative, and the drawbacks (a lasting Arcane Connection and a Warping Point for the target).
quotes: This Duration is equivalent to Moon, adding three magnitudes to a spell's base level.
If the magus does not inscribe his name into the inscription, he receives a –5 penalty.

entries.title: Ability: Rune Magic
entries.requires: Rune Magic study or Virtue: Hermetic Rune Magic
entries.summary: The Arcane Ability covering knowledge of runes: their symbolism, formulating and encrypting rune-script, and copying books on rune magic.
quotes: hiding runes, identifying rune magic, runes associated with a particular Art.

entries.title: Rune Magic and Creo Spells
entries.summary: Special rules for Creo with rune magic: created targets need the runes on an Arcane Connection to the target and are only created if it does not already exist, and healing runes take the place of natural healing while they remain on the target.
quotes: If the effect creates a target, the runes must be written on an Arcane Connection to that target, and the target is only created if it does not already exist.

gated.title: Traditions of the Tribunals
gated.intro: Hedge traditions described in the Tribunal books.

entries.title: Storm Wizards (hedge tradition)
entries.summary: Introduces the Transylvanian storm wizards, a rare Gifted hedge tradition whose apprentices are found as exposed infants on mountain slopes and taken by storm giants. Almost all are male and live alone in caves above the snowline.
quotes: The Transylvanian storm wizards are an old but lonely Gifted tradition.

entries.title: Storm Wizards and the Order
entries.summary: Explains how the Order of Hermes regards storm wizards: few know of them, the join-or-die Code provision technically applies because they are Gifted, and some joined House Ex Miscellanea during the Schism War.
quotes: As storm wizards are Gifted, the "join or die" provisions of the Code technically apply to them.

entries.title: Storm Wizards and Giants (Giant Blood and the mystery initiation)
entries.summary: Storm wizards get the Giant Blood Virtue free, earned by a mystery initiation at the end of apprenticeship in which the apprentice slays a giant and eats its heart. Powers are usable as soon as the Gift is opened, before the initiation.
quotes: If you are making a storm wizard character, this Virtue is free.
storm wizards undergo a mystery initiation in which they must slay a true giant and eat his heart

entries.title: Heart of the Storm Initiation
entries.requires: Initiation: Heart of the Storm (Storm Wizards)
entries.summary: Sidebar giving the initiation ease factor, initiation total formula and script bonus for the storm wizard initiation that grants Giant Blood.
quotes: Initiation Ease Factor: 21
Presence + Organization Lore: Storm Wizards + Script Bonus

entries.title: Storm Wizard Magic
entries.summary: Overview of storm wizard magic: exclusively Gifted, Magic-realm powers built on three Supernatural Abilities, an Arcane Ability and a seasonal activity called ice harvesting.
quotes: Their magic consists of three favored Supernatural Abilities: Storm Calling, Storm Riding, and Storm Fighting.

entries.title: Storm Wizard Virtues and Abilities
entries.summary: Sidebar explaining that storm wizards gain their Supernatural Abilities at Score 0 when the Gift is opened, and giving the Storm Calling, Storm Riding and Storm Fighting Virtues, the free Storm Wizard status and the Organization Lore: Storm Wizard Arcane Ability.
quotes: Opening Total is generated as Intelligence + Organization Lore: Storm Wizards

entries.title: Storm Calling (Supernatural Ability)
entries.summary: Supernatural Ability to create or move a storm: a roll against an Ease Factor set by the storm's size and duration, plus Auram vis sacrificed to create one. Created storms are natural once formed, and moving one costs no vis.
quotes: Storm Calling Roll: Communication + Storm Calling + Stress Die vs Ease Factor
It takes a number of rounds equal to the required Ease Factor for the storm to manifest.

entries.title: Storm Calling Ease Factors (storm size, duration and vis cost)
entries.summary: Sidebar table of the Ease Factor modifiers for storm size and duration and the Auram vis cost per size, with a worked example of creating and moving a provincial storm.
quotes: The Base Ease Factor for creating and moving a storm is 0.

entries.title: Penetration with Storm Wizard Powers
entries.summary: How Penetration is figured for storm wizard powers, using the effect roll minus the Ease Factor plus a Penetration Bonus built as for Hermetic magi, with access to the Penetration Ability.
quotes: Penetration: Storm Wizard Effect Roll – Ease Factor + Penetration Bonus

entries.title: Magnitude of Storm Wizard Effects
entries.summary: States how to determine the magnitude of a storm wizard power when it matters, for example for Warping or dispelling.
quotes: Magnitude: Storm Wizard Supernatural Ability Score

entries.title: Realm Interaction for Storm Wizard Powers
entries.summary: Storm wizard powers are Magical Supernatural Abilities and take bonuses or penalties from the local aura per the Realm Interaction Table.

entries.title: Storm Trance: Warping
entries.summary: When a storm wizard gains Warping Points, a Storm Trance roll may turn him into a local-sized storm for a Moon, during which he cannot use his powers and can try daily to reform. Failure to reform can kill him or send him into the Magic Realm.
quotes: Storm Trance Roll: Strength + Stress Die
Storm Trance Ease Factor: 3 + Warping Score

entries.title: Inside the Storm
entries.summary: Rule of thumb for deciding when a character counts as within a storm for storm wizard powers: being rained on or blown about by it, not merely being inside a building.

entries.title: Storm Riding (Supernatural Ability)
entries.summary: Supernatural Ability to sense from, or instantly travel to, any point in a visible storm (or send another character there), with a +3 bonus when the wizard is inside the storm and three ease factors by effect.
quotes: Storm Riding Roll: Perception + Storm Riding + Stress Die vs Ease Factor
he receives a +3 bonus to the Storm Riding roll if he is actually inside the storm when he uses the Ability

entries.title: Storm Fighting (Supernatural Ability)
entries.summary: Supernatural Ability to attack with a storm, with five attack types (Buffet, Deluge, Hail, Erosion, Lightning), each with its own Ease Factor, area, damage and Penetration rules.
quotes: Storm Fighting Roll: Strength + Storm Fighting + Stress Die vs Ease Factor
Lightning: Ease Factor 12.

entries.title: Ice Harvesting (seasonal activity)
entries.summary: A season-long ritual that gathers the magical non-melting ice storm wizards need as Auram vis to call storms, gathered at secret mountain sites. The vis yield comes from a formula using Intelligence, Organization Lore and the Magic aura.
quotes: (Intelligence + Organization Lore: Storm Wizard + Magic Aura) / 3 (round up) pawns of Auram vis per season

entries.title: Vampire Hunters
entries.summary: Introduces vampire hunters as specially touched humans whose magic works on all supernatural creatures, who arise by birth circumstances, vampire parentage or Hermetic training (fector).

entries.title: The Sabotnik (Saturday-born hunters)
entries.requires: Born on a Saturday or during the Unclean Days or Wolf Holiday
entries.summary: Describes the sabotnik, who is born on a Saturday and so is immune to the direct powers of vampires bound by that taboo, can sense vampires and magicians, and may be fated to become a vampire. Notes the option to randomly determine birth days.
quotes: Anyone born on a Saturday is therefore immune to the direct powers of such vampire.

entries.title: The Glog (vampire-protecting hunters)
entries.requires: Born feet first, with teeth or with red hair
entries.summary: Describes the glog, a hunter specialising in protecting people from vampires, who crafts defensive weapons from black hawthorn and is usually aggressive and physically gifted.

entries.title: Black Hawthorn (Shape and Material Bonuses)
entries.summary: Sidebar giving the Shape and Material bonuses of black hawthorn for enchanting, notably a protection-from-vampires bonus.
quotes: Protection from vampires +7 Protection from evil +4 Prevent disease +4

entries.title: The Dhampir (child of a vampire)
entries.requires: Being a child of a vampire (Dhampir Virtue)
entries.summary: Describes dhampiri, the hunters sired by vampires, who charge a fee that by tradition cannot be bargained down and who will themselves rise as vampires after death unless precautions are taken.
quotes: dhampiri carry a dark secret: that they themselves will become vampires following their death

entries.title: The Vampirdzhi (son of a vampire)
entries.summary: Describes vampirdzhia, sons of vampires who become hunters out of necessity rather than tradition, may be trained, and also risk rising as vampires after death.
quotes: Only men are believed to be vampirdzhia; the daughters of vampires become witches instead.

entries.title: Hunters' Arts (Practice and Foe Arts)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Overview of the Hunters' Arts, a splintered hedge tradition with three Practice Arts (Scry, Ban, Slay) each paired with a Foe Art. Explains how the Arts are bought as Virtues, how the first Foe Art comes free, how experience is gained and why most hunters can only use their Arts on one kind of foe.
quotes: There are three Practices that are akin to Hermetic Techniques: Scry, Ban, and Slay.

Practice Arts are bought as Major Supernatural Virtues, whereas Foe Arts are Minor Supernatural Virtues, but a character buying his first Practice Art as a Virtue gets one free Foe Art at no additional Virtue point cost.

entries.title: The Hunters' Arts and Mortal Foes
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Sidebar explaining that Hunters' Arts also work on humans and creatures aligned to a Realm but lacking Might, at a raised effect level.
quotes: Against such mortal foes, the levels of all effects are 10 higher.

entries.title: Penetration and the Hunters' Arts
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Gives the Penetration Total formula used by every Hunters' Art and notes that hunters rely on Arcane and sympathetic connections to foes.
quotes: Penetration Total: Art Total + Penetration Bonus – Level

entries.title: (Foe) Art (Virtue and rules for Foe Arts)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Describes the Foe Art Virtue: what counts as a valid foe, the storyguide's say over its breadth, and that Foe Arts are Difficult Arts that advance like Abilities and must be combined with a Practice Art.
quotes: A foe must have some supernatural power: wholly mundane groups cannot be foes.
(Foe) Arts are Difficult Arts, meaning that they are treated as any other Art except that they use the Ability Advancement Table rather than the Art Advancement Table.

entries.title: Connections to a Foe (sympathetic and arcane connection tables)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art
entries.summary: Sidebar tables of extra sympathetic connection bonuses and arcane connection durations and multipliers commonly used in the Hunters' Arts, such as names, wounds, graves and the vampire's children.
quotes: in addition to those in ArM5, page 84

entries.title: Hunter Characters
entries.summary: Character-creation guidance for sabotnici, glogove, kresnici, taltós, dhampiri and vampirdzhia: suggested Virtues, Flaws, Arts and Abilities, and a note that the Gift is not required.
quotes: Sabotnici and glogove characters should have the Second Sight Virtue, and possibly the Magic Sensitivity Virtue in addition.
Dhampir and vampirdzhi characters should take the Dhampir Virtue (see earlier) to represent their vampire ancestry.

entries.title: Scry Art: Forging the Initial Connection
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Scry
entries.summary: How a hunter makes a Scry roll to connect to a foe, with a table of Scry Levels giving direction, senses and sympathetic bonuses by strength, Range and mortal-foe adjustments, botch consequences, and how connections are replaced or cancelled.
quotes: Scry Total: Perception + Scry + (Foe) + Aura bonus + stress die
Add 10 levels (not magnitudes) if the foe lacks a Might score.

entries.title: Scry Art: Using the Scrying Connection
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Scry
entries.summary: Once a connection exists the hunter concentrates for a round and makes a non-magical roll against an Ease Factor set by the foe's strength to sense it.
quotes: Sense a Foe: Stamina + Concentration + stress die
Ease Factor: 6 + (foe's Might/5)

entries.title: Scry Art: Exploitation of Scry by a Foe
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Scry
entries.summary: How a foe may detect and exploit a scryer's connection: an Awareness roll against a falling Ease Factor, and then using Eye, Sight or Arcane range powers on the scryer through an Arcane Connection.
quotes: The Ease Factor starts at 12, but decreases by 1 every time the scryer uses her connection to find the foe.

entries.title: Ban Art (warding amulets overview)
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Ban
entries.summary: Introduces the Ban Art and its three amulets (Physical, Supernatural and Weakening Bans), noting that only the highest Ban protects a person and that Magic Resistance can nullify an amulet.
quotes: A character cannot be protected by more than one Physical or Supernatural Ban; only the one with the highest Ban Total takes effect.

entries.title: Creating a Physical Ban
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Ban
entries.summary: Amulet that absorbs wounds from a foe: made over twelve hours with a Sun Duration, its Ban Strength is spent by wound severity per a table until exhausted, with a worked example.
quotes: Physical Ban Total: Presence + Ban + (Foe) + Aura modifier + stress die
Physical Ban Strength: Physical Ban Total – Level
It takes twelve continuous hours to create a Physical Ban, and it has a Sun Duration.

entries.title: Creating a Supernatural Ban
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Ban
entries.summary: Single-use amulet that partly protects against a foe's powers by shortening durations and forcing extra Concentration rolls, with three Levels of effect; mortal foes add to the Level.
quotes: Supernatural Ban Total: Intelligence + Ban + (Foe) + Aura modifier + stress die

entries.title: Creating a Weakening Ban
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Ban
entries.summary: Area ward laid out with prepared hawthorn stakes that suppresses a foe's Might Score while it is inside, with rules for the number of stakes, activation, the roll and Penetration.
quotes: Weakening Ban Total: Intelligence + Ban + (Foe) + Aura bonus + stress die
The minimum number of stakes is one per 16 paces of the diameter of a circle, rounded up.

entries.title: Slay Art: Making the Slaying Weapon
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Slay
entries.summary: How a hunter turns a fresh weapon into a one-use foe-slayer in a day, paying a Long Term Fatigue level, with a Slay Total, a Level lowered by correct facts about the foe and raised by wrong ones, and an Incapacitating Wound effect on a successful strike.
quotes: Slay Total: Dexterity + Slay + (Foe) + Aura + stress die
It takes one day (24 hours) of continuous work to turn a normal weapon into a tool of foe-slaying, and costs the slayer one Long Term Fatigue level.
The Level is decreased by five points (to a minimum of 5, or 15 for mortal Foes) for every correct fact about the foe that the slayer has been able to discover.

entries.title: Relevant Facts About Foes
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Slay
entries.summary: Sidebar listing the kinds of facts about a foe that count toward lowering the Slay Level.

entries.title: After Slaying
entries.requires: Virtue: a Hunters' Arts Practice Art (Scry, Ban or Slay) with a (Foe) Art - Slay
entries.summary: A slaying weapon loses all magic after it is used or after its foe dies by other means, and can never be enchanted again.

entries.title: Working Together (hunter teamwork and Hermetic cooperation)
entries.summary: Sidebar on how the different hunter types and Practice Arts complement each other, and how hunters can help Hermetic magi, for example by weakening foes so spells Penetrate more easily.
quotes: the Slay Art does not destroy the vis in a creature's body like some Perdo Vim spells can

entries.title: The Order of Odin: Norse Wizard Options
entries.requires: Storyguide decision: existence of Norse wizards
entries.summary: Leaves it to the storyguide to decide whether Norse wizards exist and how organized they are, from a Norse equivalent of the Order of Hermes to scattered weak hedge magicians, and lists the kinds of magic Norse legends attribute to them.
quotes: No single Norse magician should be capable of doing all these things.

entries.title: Fenistal: A Single-Level Magic Regio
entries.summary: The exsules' hidden base lies in the upper level of a Magic regio from which all intermediate levels have been removed by powerful magic, making it very hard to reach.
quotes: with a Magic aura of 8

entries.title: The Exsules: A Renegade Hermetic Tradition
entries.requires: Tradition: Exsules of Fenistal (outcast House Merinita)
entries.summary: Profiles the isolated Hermetic exiles outside the Order, listing the Flaws they all share from their isolation and imperfect Parma Magica, the Virtues common among them, and how their magic should feel alien to Hermetic magi.
quotes: all suffer the Weird Magic Flaw due to their isolation from the Order
all have inherited the Flawed Parma Magica Flaw

related.text: Chapter 4: The Forest (Paths through the Forest)

entries.title: Diabolai (slander rites)
entries.summary: A Greek ritual in which a character with the right (Realm) Lore spends hours slandering a locally patronizing supernatural being to force it to use one of its powers for him, rolled against an Ease Factor based on the being's Might, with consequences for failure or botch.
quotes: Diabolai: Presence + (Realm) Lore + modifiers + stress die
Ease Factor: 9 + being's (Might / 5)

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, pages 87-88 (threatening saints)

entries.title: Modifiers to Diabolai
entries.summary: Sidebar listing the situational modifiers to a diabolai roll, including bonuses for public performance, synthemata and a known True Name and penalties for recent repeats or unfamiliar targets.
quotes: Performed a diabolai in the last month: –9 Threatening an unfamiliar being: –6

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, pages 34-35 (True Names)

entries.title: Katadesmos Magic (Greek Defixio tradition)
entries.summary: The Greek form of the lost Defixio tradition, whose curses work at any range without an Arcane Connection and can be conditional triggers, and which lets non-Hermetic wizards take the Leadworker Virtue.
quotes: a wizard could enact a curse on a victim at any range without the need of an Arcane Connection

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, page 143 (Leadworker)

entries.title: Gruagachan variant for Greece
entries.summary: Suggests a Pelasgic Greek variant of the Gruagachan hedge tradition that swaps enchanted tattoos for spirit magic and access to Defixio Lore.
quotes: in exchange for losing the ability to create enchanted tattoos

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, pages 114-119 (Goetic Arts)

entries.title: The Makhai (Greek Muspelli variant)
entries.summary: Notes a Greek variant of the Muspelli wizard tradition whose sorcerers serve the monsters born of Earth to avenge the titans.
quotes: Greek sorcerers who serve the monstrous Ekhidna and Typhon

entries.title: Books of the Lector Priests (Faerie Rite Wizards)
entries.requires: Tradition: Faerie Rite Wizards (Realms of Power: Faerie)
entries.summary: Lector priests were Faerie Rite Wizards whose books of rites hold closely related effects (Evocation, Grant, Weal, Ware, Woe) performed with the Ceremony Special Ability.
quotes: all priests had the Ceremony Special Ability (page 115)

entries.title: Reading the Books of Ritual
entries.summary: How a character performs an Ancient Egyptian rite from a book: a Communication + Coptic roll against a target based on effect level, ritual preparation and purity, a required Faerie aura, and reasons rites fail.
quotes: This may require a Communication + Leadership roll against a target of 3 + 1 per required follower.
the character must make a Communication + Coptic roll of 3 + (1 per 5 levels of effect)

entries.title: Egyptian Views of Vis
entries.summary: Describes the materials the Egyptians thought held heka, such as resin, gold, iron and deformed things, which tomb robbers often discard without realizing they are vis.
quotes: Resin, for example, was thought to contain heka that could be used for preservation magic

entries.title: Heka and Faerie-Based Egyptian Magic
entries.summary: Explains heka, the Egyptian name for vis and written spells, and that Egyptian religious magic is mainly Faerie-based, so flourishes such as dawn casting and animal sacrifice were not optional.
quotes: Egyptian religious magic differed from Hermetic magic in that it is primarily based on the Faerie, not Magical, realm.

entries.title: Egyptian Rites Without Realms of Power: Faerie
entries.summary: A Hermetic substitute for Faerie Rites: after a Communication + Coptic roll, the reader makes a casting total from Stamina, closest Form and Technique, and Aura, with a table of Fatigue loss and Warping by result; Egyptian books are treated as casting tablets.
quotes: the character must make a Communication + Coptic roll against an Ease Factor of 3 + (1 per 5 levels of effect)
The speaker's casting total is: Stamina + closest Form + closest Technique + Aura + stress dice (modified by Virtues and Flaws)

entries.title: Transitory Magic Items
entries.summary: Introduces single-use items made by Faerie-aligned Egyptian magicians that are not enchanted but carry a supernatural property, commonly temporary amulets and potions.
quotes: A transitory magic item is an object which has supernatural properties, but only for a single use

entries.title: Temporary Amulets (Until Duration)
entries.summary: A temporary amulet is an object carrying a spell with the Faerie-only Until Duration that ends when the amulet is worn and discarded, and the effect survives its creator's death.
quotes: an object on which a spell with the Until Duration has been cast

entries.title: Egyptian Seals (temporary magic items)
entries.summary: Seals hold a spell maintained by an Until Duration or act like Watching Wards, triggering when a precondition (usually breaking the seal) is met.
quotes: Egyptian seals of this type are remarkably similar to Watching Wards.

entries.title: Temporary Potions
entries.summary: Potions made by pouring water or beer over a statue housing a faerie (such as a cippus of Horus) or over inscribed bowls, each giving a single effect if a nearby faerie accepts the deal.
quotes: Each statue provided a single effect.

entries.title: The Drawing of Maat (tongue magic)
entries.summary: A lost technique of painting the goddess of Truth on the tongue that prevents lying and, once its Mystery is found, creates a tiny possessing faerie that corrects mispronunciation so botches are less likely.
quotes: The faerie checks his words for mispronunciations and corrects them

entries.title: Saliva and Breath Ranges
entries.summary: Spitting or breathing on a target counts as a Range equivalent to Personal, but without bypassing Magic Resistance as Personal spells do, making some Spontaneous spells easier.
quotes: Treat this as equivalent to Personal range, but without circumventing Magic resistance as Personal spells do.

entries.title: Statue Consecration
entries.summary: How chief lectors consecrate a new statue so a faerie inhabits it, by performing a ritual narrative that faeries feed on; the roll is aided by a Faerie aura. Sidebars give examples of animated models and the play of faeries against one another.
quotes: This requires a Communication + Folk Ken roll against a target of 18.

entries.title: Unusual Amulets: Ib Scarab and Royal Names
entries.summary: The Ib Scarab replaces the heart and works at Personal Range, and seals with royal names carry a little Magic Resistance that may accidentally protect a wearer from curses.
quotes: it replaces the heart, and so can create effects at Personal Range.
These royal names have a little Magic Resistance, perhaps as high as 5 points.

entries.title: Temporary Objects From Models
entries.summary: Model objects in tombs can become temporary real objects with a faerie inside; troupes without Realms of Power: Faerie design it as a shapeshifting magic item.
quotes: Groups using only the core rules should design a magic item with a shapeshifting effect.

entries.title: Threatening the Gods
entries.summary: Describes the alternative Enchantment Faerie Rite Method in which a caster threatens to destroy a faerie and the world unless given what is demanded, and who used it.
quotes: The spell-caster threatened to destroy not only the faerie, but the entire world, unless given what was demanded.

entries.title: The Weakest and Commonest Ancient Magicians
entries.summary: Describes local-spirit priests like village witches and suggests ways to design them, such as Faerie Friend, Faerie Doctors or Faerie Bargainers, with their grave goods as Mystery quest goals.
quotes: Some of these priests of local gods could be designed as Faerie Doctors

entries.title: Writings of Those Who Threatened the Gods
entries.summary: Three kinds of recoverable texts: Enchant-scripts, threat scripts that add a bonus to a Rite's casting total, and Mystery initiation texts granting Virtues such as Puissant Enchantment.
quotes: These grant a bonus to the casting total of a particular Rite.

entries.title: Magical Craftwork
entries.summary: Introduces the caste of magical crafters who made amulets, talismans and curses, whose writings produced the Learned Magician tradition and remain usable by Coptic speakers.

entries.title: Egyptian Craft Magic and Learned Magic
entries.requires: Learned Magician rules (Hedge Magic: Revised Edition)
entries.summary: Shows how to simulate Ancient Egyptian amulets, talismans and curses with Learned Magic Techniques and Forms, noting that Egyptian magic lacks the Range, Target and Duration limits and Difficult Arts, and assumes high casting and lab totals.
quotes: Troupes using the Learned Magician rules to create Egyptian spells should assume that the Egyptians had very high casting and laboratory totals

entries.title: Contained Spirits
entries.summary: Rules of thumb for creatures trapped in containers: bargains bind only the words spoken, a spirit can be won as a permanent ally by favors comparable to Mystery Ordeals, and freeing a faerie unconditionally invites a gift in return.
quotes: A bargain struck with these beings is binding, but only the specific words, not the intent, need to be adhered to.
A rescued spirit may be converted into a permanent ally by performing a series of favors for it.

entries.title: A Note on True Names
entries.summary: Explains Egyptian casualness about True Names (ka names, rens) listed in tombs and how shabti servants answer the name and shift the target of curses.
quotes: The owner had shabtis, little statue servants, who answered his True Name for him.

entries.title: The Book of Thoth
entries.summary: A character who reads the Book of Thoth can effortlessly cast almost any Hermetic spell but dies or fades into Twilight within a day, after which the Book is hidden again.
quotes: Within one day, however, they either die or fade into Twilight.
